content:
Apple is set to launch several new Macs later this year, including the first MacBook with a touchscreen, the first models powered by the M6 chip, and more. Here's everything we know so far about the upcoming new Macs.

MacBook Ultra

The flagship Mac launching later this year will be the first Mac to feature a touchscreen. Whether this new machine will be called the MacBook Pro or MacBook Ultra remains undecided, but it will mark the most significant overhaul of the MacBook Pro in years.

Apple is reportedly testing a high-end MacBook model with macOS 27.1, with an official launch expected by the end of October.

This new MacBook model will be Apple's first notebook to feature both a touchscreen and an OLED display. It's also expected to ditch the notch in favour of a Dynamic Island-style design similar to the iPhone. According to Bloomberg, the new high-end MacBook will also be thinner than the current MacBook Pro.

In terms of performance, the new touchscreen MacBook will use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the current MacBook Pro lineup.

M6 MacBook

Apple is reportedly planning to launch its first M6-powered Mac later this year. The company is working on an updated entry-level MacBook Pro featuring the next-generation M6 processor.

According to reports, the M6 will offer faster memory bandwidth along with improvements in CPU and GPU core performance.

Aside from the M6 chip, the new entry-level MacBook Pro is not expected to see any other changes.

iMac

Apple last updated the 24-inch iMac in October 2024, when it bumped the chip from M3 to M4. Apple is now working on the next-generation iMac update, reportedly set for release this autumn.

The new iMac is expected to feature Apple's upcoming M6 chip. There are also rumours that the new iMac will offer a fresh lineup of colour options.

Mac mini and Mac Studio (Maybe)

Lastly, Apple is also working on updates to the Mac mini and Mac Studio, though the release dates for these two machines remain unclear.

For the Mac mini, Apple is reportedly testing a new product line featuring M5 Pro and entry-level M6 chips. As for the Mac Studio, versions with M5 Max and M5 Ultra processors are being tested.

According to Bloomberg, the release timeline for these machines is not yet clear and will depend on "memory chip supply conditions." The general expectation outside had been for a new Mac Studio to launch before the end of this year, but that now appears to be up in the air.

For reference, the current Mac mini is available with M4 and M4 Pro chips, while the Mac Studio offers M4 Max and M3 Ultra configuration options.

Conclusion

Apple's Mac lineup is currently in a somewhat awkward position due to memory and storage chip supply constraints across the industry. That said, the company still has a fairly strong lineup of new models in the pipeline. What are your thoughts on the new Macs launching before the end of this year? What do you think the MacBook Ultra will be priced at? Let us know in the comments.
